errors: Never compares 4.1 over the same days or looks for backend/remote-config causes, so a non-client cause would be chased in the app diff
Play rollout widened after only 'a few hours' at 10-20% with no minimum sample
R2-A.why: Well ordered and proportionate, with containment, symbolication, store consoles, the upgrade path and a one-day revert timebox, but it takes for granted that 4.2 is the cause and its rollout gate is thin.

R2-B.why: Catches nearly every trap with concrete actions: metric artefact check, 4.1/backend check, upgrade-path repro, revert timebox, 5/20/50/100 with 24h gates and a 99.5% target. Only adoption tracking is light, and the per-stage sample is by time alone.

errors: No upgrade-from-4.1 reproduction, so a migration crash may not reproduce
Does not check whether 4.2 changed the Sentry SDK or session counting
R2-C.why: Strongest on 'is it 4.2 at all' with clear branches, server-side mitigation, evidence preservation, numeric rollout gates and an explicit revert fallback rule. It misses the upgrade-path repro and the instrumentation-change check; adding an error boundary to the hotfix is slight scope creep.

errors: No timebox for reverting versus continuing to debug
Stop rule compares 4.2.1 against 4.2 rather than 4.1, a weak bar for halting
R2-D.why: Very disciplined: symbolication in step 0 from the original CI artefacts, SDK-change check, 4.1 comparison, proof-by-revert, a sample-based stage rule and an explicit step to move users off 4.2. It lacks a revert deadline and the upgrade-path test.

errors: No explicit comparison of 4.1's crash rate over the same days
No timebox for revert versus fix
Promotion gate sample size left as 'meaningful'
R2-E.why: Solid and well grounded (symbols first, good slicing including fresh versus upgrade, store consoles, backend timeline, staged hotfix with a 99.5% gate), but several key items are stated loosely and there is no decision deadline.

errors: No timebox for revert versus fix
Store consoles are used for cross-checking, but it never says Sentry misses pre-init/native crashes
R2-F.why: Tight plan with a check on every step: metric-definition and SDK-change check, 4.1 same-days comparison, proof-by-revert on a release build, a stop rule with a sample, and a careful move-users-off-4.2 step. Gaps are the revert deadline and the upgrade path.

errors: No comparison of 4.1 over the same days; backend change appears only as a diff bullet
Rollout gate sample is only 'enough sessions'
Upgrade path is segmented but not reproduced by upgrading from 4.1
R2-G.why: Clear, proportionate and correctly ordered, with a hard one-day revert timebox and an adoption follow-up, but verification and the is-it-really-4.2 check are thinner than in the top plans.

errors: Shipping 4.1's code over 4.2 installs does not consider persisted-state/schema downgrade risk
Does not check whether 4.2 changed the Sentry SDK or session counting
R2-H.why: Concrete first steps with queries and diffs, a dated decision point for a revert build with a backend-compatibility check, and numeric, sample-based stop criteria. It misses the upgrade path and the instrumentation check, and adoption is only 'keep prompting'.
